message.content:
**Killing Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from the Command Prompt**

On Windows you can terminate an application by its image name (`/IM`) or by its process ID (`/PID`).  
For VS Code the executable is called **code.exe**.

---

### 1️⃣ Kill *all* running instances of VS Code

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM code.exe` – matches any process whose image name is `code.exe`.
* `/F` – forces termination (equivalent to “End Process” in Task Manager).

This will close every instance of VS Code that is currently running.

---

### 2️⃣ Kill a specific instance by PID

If you only want to close one particular window:

1. Find the PID first:

   ```cmd
   tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
   ```

   This lists all `code.exe` processes and their PIDs.

2. Terminate the chosen PID:

   ```cmd
   taskkill /PID <PID_NUMBER> /F
   ```

   Replace `<PID_NUMBER>` with the actual number shown in the list.

---

### 3️⃣ Common pitfalls & tips

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| “Access is denied.” | Run CMD as Administrator (right‑click → “Run as administrator”). |
| “No tasks are running which match the specified criteria.” | Make sure VS Code is actually running; check the exact image name (`code.exe`, not `Code.exe`). |
| You want to keep certain windows open | Use the PID method instead of `/IM`. |

---

### 4️⃣ Quick one‑liner (if you’re already inside a script)

```cmd
for /f "tokens=2 delims=," %i in ('tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe" /FO CSV /NH') do taskkill /PID %i /F
```

*(In a batch file replace `%i` with `%%i`.)*

---

#### TL;DR

```cmd
:: Close every VS Code window
taskkill /IM code.exe /F

:: Or close a specific one
taskkill /PID 12345 /F
```

That’s it! 🎉
